crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Routing Across Automated Market Makers
children.blurb: Routing across automated market makers covers the process of finding and executing a trade through one or more on-chain liquidity pools to achieve the best available outcome.

children.name: Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts
children.blurb: Yield strategies in smart contracts are automated programs that move deposited capital across decentralised finance protocols to earn returns from lending, liquidity provision, staking, and arbitrage.

children.name: On-Chain Forensics
children.blurb: On-chain forensics is the practice of examining blockchain transaction records to trace the movement of digital assets, attribute addresses to real-world entities, and reconstruct financial activity across crypto markets and decentralised finance protocols.

children.name: Stablecoin Stress Testing
children.blurb: Stablecoin stress testing examines how a stablecoin maintains its peg and meets redemptions under adverse market conditions, including runs, collateral devaluation, liquidity freezes, and operational failures.

children.name: Governance Token Outcomes
children.blurb: Governance token outcomes refers to the measurable results of holding and using tokens that confer voting rights in decentralized protocols, including price performance, voting participation, treasury allocation, and protocol changes.

sections.body: This field examines how AI systems are used in crypto markets and decentralised finance. It covers exchange routing, yield strategies, on-chain forensics, stablecoin stress and governance tokens. In practice, AI models read order books, mempool data, smart contract events, and governance forums. They help route trades across automated market makers, estimate yield, flag suspicious wallet behavior, and simulate stablecoin runs. The work is often about pattern recognition and optimization under uncertainty, not about predicting prices with certainty. It also studies how automated agents interact with transparent but adversarial blockchain environments.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts of this field are relatively mature, while others remain experimental. Routing across automated market makers is a live engineering problem with measurable slippage and gas costs, and on-chain forensics has real tools for clustering addresses and tracing flows, though mixers, privacy coins, and cross-chain bridges create gaps. Yield strategies in smart contracts can be automated, but returns depend on liquidity, incentives, and contract risk. Stablecoin stress testing remains hard because reserves, redemption behavior, and market confidence are not fully observable. Governance token outcomes are especially unsettled, since token voting, delegation, and treasury decisions often diverge from stated decentralization. Honest limits include data quality, adversarial manipulation, and the fact that backtests rarely capture a true crisis, and the site's 215 compliance and regulation pages are a companion reference for the rules that shape all of this.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages in this section build from mechanics to risk to governance. Routing Across Automated Market Makers explains how trades are split and executed across pools, which is the base layer for market activity. Yield Strategies in Smart Contracts looks at how automated positions chase returns and what risks those strategies carry. On-Chain Forensics covers the investigative side, tracing wallets, exploits, and illicit flows. Stablecoin Stress Testing examines what happens when a peg is tested and how models try to measure that pressure. Governance Token Outcomes closes the section by asking whether token-based voting changes real decisions or mostly records them, and a reader can move through the pages in that order or jump to the one that matches a specific question.
